stories.title: Gears of War: E-Day Studio Boss Insists 'The Next Game Will Not Take Nearly as Long' to Make, Responds to Layoff Concern
stories.summary: The boss of Gears of War: E-Day developer The Coalition has responded to reports that staff at the studio are worried they will lose their jobs amid the ongoing cuts at Xbox, and promised the next Gears game won’t take as long to make.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Gears of War: E-Day Studio Boss Insists 'The Next Game Will Not Take Nearly as Long' to Make, Responds to Layoff Concern
sources.text: The boss of Gears of War: E-Day developer The Coalition has responded to reports that staff at the studio are worried they will lose their jobs amid the ongoing cuts at Xbox, and promised the next Gears game won’t take as long to make. Earlier this month, Eurogamer reported on serious internal concern that layoffs would hit The Coalition after the release of E-Day. "The mood is certainly 'let's not celebrate the game until we're three months post launch, just in case,' which is very unusual," one source told the site. "We're just expecting the next wave [of layoffs], or being reorganized under Activision or something later this year," claimed another. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma’s “reset” of Microsoft’s gaming business has seen nearly 2,000 people cut already this financial year, with more to come. A number of studios have left the business or are in the process of closing down. Microsoft has also reorganized its studios, bringing Halo and Sea of Thieves developer Rare under Call of Duty developer Activision, and Grounded developer Obsidian under Fallout developer Bethesda. The Coalition has, for the most part, avoided the cuts, although E-Day's story director was laid off just one week before the game's early access launch . The BBC put Eurogamer’s report to The Coalition studio head Mike Crump, who danced around the issue in his response. "What I say to myself, what I say to the team, is we need to focus on the things that we can control,” Crump said. "For us that's about shipping a great game that people are going to love and I feel like, as a team, we've done that." No guarantee, then, that The Coalition will escape the fate suffered by so many at Xbox this summer. But Crump did suggest there are plans for more Gears of War games. He called E-Day a "great foundation" for future games in the series, and said "the next game will not take nearly as long" to make. As for what the next Gears game is, in June 2024, Microsoft pledged to continue the story of Gears of War and wrap up the cliffhanger posed by Gears 5's ending, despite creating a prequel first with E-Day. The question is, will The Coalition get the chance to make it? Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

sources.title: Gears Of War Boss Dodges Question About Future Layoffs, Promises Next Game Will Come Sooner
sources.text: Xbox is currently in the middle of its big corporate “reset, ” which has involved the company shuffling around franchises and teams while it continues to lay off workers . And while this has all been happening, The Coalition launched Gears of War: E-Day , a well-received Xbox-exclusive prequel to the original trilogy. Many are wondering what the studio’s future holds. Coalition studio head Mike Crump says the team is focused on what it “can control.” In a new interview with the BBC, Crump was directly asked about the recent Eurogamer report that claimed numerous Coalition devs remained nervous about the Xbox laying off staff after shipping E-Day . The studio boss didn’t share any details about the studio’s immediate future or if cuts were coming, and instead suggested the goal is just to make good games people like. He even promised that the next Gears game won’t take seven years to arrive like this one did. “What I say to myself, what I say to the team, is we just need to focus on the things that we can control,” said Crump. “For us that’s about shipping a great game that people are going to love, and I feel like, as a team, we’ve done that.” According to Crump, E-Day is a “great foundation” for future Gears titles, and he told the BBC that “the next game will not take nearly as long” to create. He then added something that sounds almost like Crump is trying to convince any Xbox leadership listening to not to make cuts to the studio , as it would disrupt the decades of experience the team has built up since it took over Gears of War back in 2014. “We’ve got a great team here. And the leadership team in particular has worked together for upwards of 20 years,” said Crump. “So there’s definitely a continuity of knowledge and experience.” The Coalition has mostly dodged Xbox’s layoffs , though the game’s story director and others were laid off last month , as Kotaku reported. sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: Gears of War boss says the next game won't take seven years to make as he dances around the question of layoffs
sources.text: The Coalition, the Microsoft-owned studio behind Gears of War: E-Day, Gears 4 and Gears 5 has mostly survived the wide-ranging cuts and layoffs initiated by Xbox CEO Asha Sharma in her attempt to bring the gaming division back to profitability . But as Eurogamer reported, now that Gears of War: E-Day has shipped, many within The Coalition fear they're going to be laid off shortly afterwards , potentially missing out on bonuses. Now, in an interview with the BBC , studio head Mike Crump was asked about the report and whether cuts are planned for the Canadian studio. Crump didn't offer specifics about the future of the studio, however. "What I say to myself, what I say to the team, is we just we need to focus on the things that we can control," said Crump. "For us that's about shipping a great game that people are going to love and I feel like, as a team, we've done that." E-Day has been fairly well-received by critics and embraced by players, boasting the series' best numbers on Steam . In the Eurogamer E-Day campaign review , Dom Peppiatt said the game proves there's still life left in the aging franchise. But the big question is whether that is going to be enough to keep The Coalition safe and convince Xbox to invest in a future project. E-Day is an Xbox console exclusive - a decision reportedly hastily made just before the game's big summer reveal - which limits its audience and sales potential. "Gears has been an exclusive franchise to Xbox for 20 years now. It's sort of entwined deeply with the brand," said Crump. Asked how the studio measures success, the studio head said that while numbers are important, there's more that gets taken into account. Said Crump, "We measure things like, are we showcasing the platform? Are we pushing the hardware to its limits? Are we showcasing what the Xbox is capable of? "Our goal basically is to be the best-looking game on the Xbox and really show the industry what's possible with our hardware." After shipping Gears 5 in 2019, it took The Coalition seven years to develop and release Gears of War: E-Day. To that end, the studio boss believes E-Day makes for a "great foundation" for future sequels, and promises the next game "will not take nearly as long" to develop. The Coalition has not announced any future projects.

Last week a report suggested that employees at The Coalition were worried they may be laid off immediately following the game’s release. Now, in an interview with the BBC, studio head Mike Crump says his message to the team has been to continue doing their best because things like layoffs are out of their control. “What I say to myself, what I say to the team, is we just we need to focus on the things that we can control,” Crump said. “For us that’s about shipping a great game that people are going to love and I feel like, as a team, we’ve done that.” He added: “We’ve got a great team here. And the leadership team in particular has worked together for upwards of 20 years. So there’s definitely a continuity of knowledge and experience.” Crump also stated that E-Day, which was largely built from scratch instead of building on top of previous Gears titles, will provide “a great foundation” for future entries in the series, meaning “the next game will not take nearly as long to make”. Last week Eurogamer cited sources who told it Xbox âs decision to lay off story director Juan Vaca two weeks before the gameâs release was “very demoralising” for the development team at The Coalition. Another source raised concern that if staff are laid off soon, they may miss out on a contracted bonus which is paid out should the game reach a certain score on Metacritic (something that’s almost certainly set to be paid, given that it currently sits at a Metacritic score of 87). In terms of pure gunplay, however, very little beats it this year.â

stories.summary: Star Wars Zero Company released in late August to great reviews, but its launch was bittersweet, as a large chunk of developer Bit Reactor's staff was furloughed , unsure if they would be returning to work. For at least a portion of them, however, that uncertainty is over, as they're back at the studio. Speaking to Game File , Bit Reactor CEO Greg Foertsch said the studio had "started the process...

sources.title: Star Wars Zero Company Developer Sees Portion Of Furloughed Workers Return

sources.name: GamesIndustry.biz
sources.title: Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor begins bringing furloughed staff back
sources.text: One source says more than half of the pre-furlough team is now back on the payroll Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has started bringing back staff it furloughed ahead of the game's launch. In a statement shared on Bluesky , CEO Greg Foertsch said the studio "started the process of returning more of our team back to work" this week, but stopped short of confirming how many people are returning. Foertsch said asking staff to step away was "an incredibly difficult decision" that followed "unexpected business developments outside of our control," but was necessary to "eventually bring as many people back as possible." A person familiar with the situation told Game File that more than half of the pre-furlough team is now back on the payroll, with others still unpaid. Game File has reported that furloughed staff keep their employee status but receive neither salary nor benefits. Bit Reactor furloughed "many of its workers" in the weeks before the game's release, a decision it said was made "before it was clear how the launch would go." Sources told Game File at the time that 80% of staff were furloughed, leaving a skeleton crew to address post-launch bugs.

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Bit Reactor CEO Welcomes Return of Some Furloughed Staff for 'Continued Support' of Star Wars Zero Company
sources.text: Bit Reactor, the developer of Star Wars Zero Company, has begun returning some of its staff to the team after furloughing an estimated 80% of employees just before the game’s launch. Bit Reactor’s CEO Greg Foertsch revealed the news in a public post on October 7, where he explained that the furloughs were necessary to “help us eventually bring as many people back as possible.” Foertsh said that bringing these staff members back to Bit Reactor was an “important step forward” in the studio’s “continued support for Zero Company,” and that the team looks forward to sharing more updates about the game “soon.” “Having to ask team members to step away after we navigated unexpected business developments outside of our control and so close to launch was an incredibly difficult decision,” Foertsh wrote. “...This team means a tremendous amount to me, and I am incredibly proud of what we have accomplished together. Thank you to our fans for the incredible response to the game and for supporting us along this journey.” Sources with information about the situation told GameFile that the number of Bit Reactor’s payrolled staff now account for “more than half of what it had been ahead of the furloughs,” meaning that there is still a sizeable chunk of furloughed staff who aren’t getting paid. Star Wars Zero Company launched in August 2026 to rave reviews, getting a sparkling nine out of 10 from our reviewers here at IGN who praised it for being an “excellent tactical game that does a fantastic job of slathering on the same cinematic look and feel we saw in Respawn's Star Wars Jedi games, incorporating strong characters and a storyline that's refreshingly centered on non-Force users and a non-traditional villain.” Despite its success, much of Bit Reactor’s staff were placed on leave without pay just before Zero Company launched, with reports indicating around 80% of employees were affected. This has become a recurring trend within the game development industry, to the point where Gears of War: E-Day developers were overcome with worry that they would get laid off after “crunching hard” to get the game out on time. This is the latest news to get revealed about Zero Company after GameFile uncovered legal documents revealing that the game was initially pitched as a title within the Titanfall universe , with specific connections to Apex Legends . While this pitch ultimately didn’t go through, it’s certainly intriguing enough to make us wonder what such a game would have looked like, had it actually been made. Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

sources.name: GamesRadar
sources.title: Star Wars Zero Company studio is "returning" furloughed developers after "incredible response"
sources.text: "We look forward to sharing more updates regarding Bit Reactor and Zero Company" Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor is actively "returning more of our team back to work" after furloughing staff right before launch due to apparent budget issues. In a post on Bluesky , Bit Reactor CEO Greg Foertsch confirms the great de-furloughing began this week, which it calls "an important step in our continued support for Zero Company." The statement confirms much of what was reported around the launch. "Having to ask team members to step away after we navigated unexpected business developments out of our control and so close to launch was an incredibly difficult decision, but one that was necessary to help us eventually bring as many people back as possible," Foertsch continues. It's unclear how many, if any, developers may be laid off at the end of this return process. Whereas layoffs result in immediate job cuts, a furlough is essentially a period of unpaid absence or reduced hours which is generally enacted to lower costs and overhead during a period of some kind of financial hardship. Game File's Stephen Totilo reports "over half" of the team has now returned. "This team means a tremendous amount to me, and I am incredibly proud of what we have accomplished together," Foertsch adds. "Thank you to our fans for the incredible response to the game and for supporting us along this journey. We look forward to sharing more updates regarding Bit Reactor and Zero Company soon." Star Wars Zero Company saw some of the strongest reviews of any Star Wars game in recent years. We called it a solid strategy RPG after getting our feet wet, and it's sitting comfortably at a score of 84 on Metacritic. On Steam, Zero Company has "very positive" reviews. It was an utter shame to see the team behind it struggling even after shipping a great game, and it's good to see them getting back on their feet. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more I've learned to love Star Wars Zero Company's permadeath – by letting the new hires die . Austin has been a game journalist for 12 years, having freelanced for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, IGN, Sports Illustrated, and more while finishing his journalism degree. He's been with GamesRadar+ since 2019. They've yet to realize his position is a cover for his career-spanning Destiny column, and he's kept the ruse going with a lot of news and the occasional feature, all while playing as many roguelikes as possible. sources.name: Xbox Wire
sources.title: STAR WARS: Galactic Racer — Crashing with Consequence in Runs-Based Racing
sources.text: Allow us to set the scene. Three corners from the finish line, another racer shunts your repulsorcraft into an adjacent boulder, sending you careening into the toxic wastes of Sentinel I. You try to correct your course. Too late. The vehicle that took you 4 tours and 23 races to tune is now scattered across the track, your League Token is forfeit, and the tour is over. These are the moments that are instrumental in your journey to become Champion of the Galactic League, and the moments that the team built around STAR WARS: Galactic Racer — available today for XBOX Series X|S. “We’ve got a history of trying to make failure fun,” says Creative Director at Fuse Games Kieran Crimmins. “Failure can be this big, spectacular, exciting, interesting and rewarding experience in the game. Our wreck-out system is meant to be the ethos of how Fuse approach game making. Crashing isn’t just a big spectacle; it has consequence as well as mechanical rewards so you can learn something for your next run.” “Failure is fuel, which is where our runs-based mechanic comes into play,” adds Co-founder and Head of Content at Fuse Games Steve Uphill. “It’s the opportunity to try again, and when you get the right combination of builds, parts and upgrades, failure makes winning feel hard earned, but so much more rewarding and creates a powerful and unique player story.” In STAR WARS: Galactic Racer , player persistence is the key to success. Kieran explains what runs-based actually means, and how Fuse Games adds their own spin on the widely used term: “For us, runs-based is a replayable loop that allows you to experiment with a new way to play every time, see how far you get with it, and if you fail, you still get some great rewards to go again so you can try with a new combination of parts and abilities.” “From start to end, the process looks like this: the player starts by choosing which vehicle you want to attempt that run in, whether it be a skim speeder, speeder bike, or landspeeder. They all have slightly different playstyles and attributes. Then, you pick a Racer Style, which gives your build a baseline direction. So, if you wanted to make an afterburner build or a cooled build for example, you start with that Racer Style, then select which abilities, parts and upgrades complement it at the end of each race. Depending how well you do in the races, you’ll also get financial rewards that you can spend at the shop in between planets. There’s always going to be the temptation to try out new abilities or upgrades, but these are rewarded randomly, so there’s an element of luck involved. Most will be able to synergise with your build in some way, so it’s up to your knowledge and creativity for that limited set to find a path to success. If you’re lucky, you’ll win the league. If you don’t win the league, however, the path to success is filled with challenges, rivals, and events to test you. Crash too many times and you’ll ‘wreck out’, or you fail a high-stakes event, then you’ll lose a League Token and be back to the start.” Failure is an important part of the game’s mechanics, which is why ‘wrecking out’ is so instrumental to gameplay: “You have a certain number of crashes that you’re allowed to do in any race,” says Kieran, “not all events have it, but a lot of them do. If you use all your crashes, then you’ll ‘wreck out’ and have to start from the beginning of that tour. Crucially, we wanted there to be an element of consequence in the gameplay. Your decisions matter across every part of the game, so you need some sort of finite failure state for your decisions to matter, and wrecking out felt like a great manifestation of that. Every corner matters, every interaction with another racer matters. It forces you to think about what choices you make and what you’re doing, rather than driving with abandon.” It’s this element of player agency and choice that makes the runs-based loop in STAR WARS: Galactic Racer so satisfying. Kieran expresses the importance of player choice: “If you think about playing in its most base form, it isn’t someone tells you what to do then you do it. That’s a job, that’s instruction. Instead, we provide a play space full of fun things. Play is the choice to arrange them in the way that you want, and creating your own moments and journeys. The power of a good player story is the absolute power of play in general.” And that agency doesn’t end when the run does. Kieran continues: “There are two important progression routes for a run. The first is your stat build-up, where you get temporary stats for each vehicle like cornering, resilience, ramjet, afterburner etc. This allows you to dial into your playstyle as well as your build, and you can add points to make those base stats different. The second one is your combination of parts. As standard, you’ll get to install up to five parts. Each of those parts have different rarity, and you build those up as you go through the different events, either from the shop or as event awards. They all do vastly different things and synergise in different ways, some even develop faults that change builds even further. The combinations in the parts system is so vast, I’m not even sure we’ve seen every single combination yet!” “You also get permanent progression outside of each tour that you can put into one of your vehicle types. So, it’s the same set of stats, but they’ll stay there for the rest of your enjoyment of the game. Once you beat a tour, you open up a larger pool of parts. You’ll also unlock new ‘favors’ that you can equip to further modify the rules for the next run. Another form of permanent progression is the ability to upgrade your Racer Styles, so you can unlock all sorts of different ways to play.” These features carry over to multiplayer, too: “In multiplayer, we wanted to create a runs-based system that worked. They’re not exactly the same, because it’s a shorter session time, and we wanted people to move through it much faster. Similarly to

sources.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer Multiplayer Party Limit Will Be Doubled Via Update
sources.text: Star Wars: Galactic Racer has broadly proven to be a smash hit with critics, and fans seem similarly enthusiastic, but developer Fuse Games has heard the concern regarding multiplayer party sizes and has responded via the game’s official social media. Resultingly, it appears we should be able to expect an update to increase the multiplayer party size from three to six players at some point within the next few weeks. “Thank you so much for your feedback and we’d like to let you and everyone on this thread know that we hear you,” the developer responded to various fans raising the concern online. “We’re working on an update to increase the party size from three to six players, with the aim of releasing it within the first few weeks of launch.” More details will be available soon, the developer noted. IGN’s Star Wars: Galactic Racer review called it “a fabulous looking and frantically fast anti-grav racer… that has successfully lit the afterburners on a long-dormant slice of the Star Wars universe.” Luke Reilly is an award-winning journalist with 23 years of media experience across Official PlayStation Magazine, Australian 360, and IGN – which he joined in 2011. You can find him on Bluesky @mrlukereilly to ask him things about stuff.

sources.name: Video Games Chronicle
sources.title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer will double the game’s multiplayer party limit in an upcoming patch
sources.text: The game currently supports parties of 3 players Star Wars: Galactic Racer developer Fuse Games has announced that the game’s multiplayer party limit will be doubled in an upcoming update. At the time of writing, Star Wars: Galactic Racer ‘s multiplayer parties are currently limited to three players, a limitation that was met with dissapointment from players who wanted to play with more of their friends. Now, in a social media post, the Star Wars: Galactic Racer account has confirmed that this restriction will be eased in a future update. Responding to a fan on X , the account wrote, “Thank you so much for your feedback and we’d like to let you and everyone on this thread know that we hear you! We’re working on an update to increase the party size from 3 to 6 players, with the aim of releasing it within the first few weeks of launch. More details coming soon!” Thank you so much for your feedback and we'd like to let you and everyone on this thread know that we hear you! We're working on an update to increase the party size from 3 to 6 players, with the aim of releasing it within the first few weeks of launch. More details coming soon! While no specific date for this update was shared, it should comes as good news to fans. Star Wars: Galactic Racer has been met with critical acclaim and strong player support, but issues like the lack of private multiplayer races, and this small party restriction remain. VGC’s review of the game called it a “modern racing classic” that “absolutely nails what it is trying to do”. “It is a high-octane racer that’s endless fun to play, and it looks fantastic,” we said. “This would have been a great game with a standard single-player mode, but what is here is inventive and engaging. I’d have loved a few silly classic characters and another planet or two, but this is a game I’ll return to for a long time.” Star Wars: Galactic Racer was released earlier this week. At the time of writing, players with Amazon Prime can play the single-player portion of the game via Amazon’s Luna service at no extra cost. “We’ve always believed Luna players deserve to be in the action from day one, and Star Wars: Galactic Racer makes that a reality for the first time,” Amazon head of gaming Jeff Gattis told GamesIndustry.biz in a statement.

sources.title: Forza Horizon 6 isn’t coming to PS5 this year, it’s claimed
sources.text: Forza Horizon 6 is currently scheduled for 2026, according to Playground Games Forza Horizon 6 won’t come to PlayStation this year after all, it’s claimed. Developer Playground Games , as recently as last month, claimed that the critically acclaimed Xbox and PC racer would still arrive this year, as previously announced by Xbox. However, a new report disputes that. According to Deallabs writer billbul-kun , who has been accurately reporting hardware and software release information for a number of years now, the PS5 port of the Playground Games racer won’t arrive on PlayStation until 2027. Billbul-kun claims that Forza Horizon 6 will be released on PlayStation 5 on January 26. The report goes on to claim that a physical version of the game will also be released, though it’s unknown if the game’s Premium Edition will come to PlayStation. In September, Playground Games claimed that the game was still due this year.Â “If youâre planning your trip to Discover Japan on PlayStation 5, stay tuned,” a statement on the game’s official website read in an update posted last month. “Forza Horizon 6 will be releasing on PS5 later this year, and you can add the game to your Wishlist on the PlayStation Store to be notified of availability,” it added. Playground Games has never set a firm date on the PS5 version, only that it would come sometime after the PC and Xbox launch, which took place earlier this year. VGCâs Forza Horizon 6 review called it âan essential racing gameâ, and said developer Playground Games had outdone itself. â Forza Horizon 5 was already an exceptional racing game, but Forza Horizon 6 takes everything up a notch to deliver an even more engaging, entertaining and all-encompassing experience,â we said. âThereâs an absolute wealth of racing, exploring and collecting to do here, and thatâs before the inevitable live-service updates start adding even more content. Few games are as essential as this.â

sources.title: Forza Horizon 6 has been delayed on PS5, a new report suggests, not long after developer Playground insisted it hadn't
sources.text: Forza Horizon 6 's highly-anticipated release on PlayStation 5 has apparently been delayed to 2027, according to new information. Yes, this is not the first time we've heard that - The Verge's Tom Warren and IGN said as much in late August . Forza Horizon 6 studio Playground Games countered those claims days later, however, saying the open-world driving game has not been pushed back , while opening wishlisting for it on the PlayStation Store. Now, Dealabs' reliable leaker billbil-kun has added their voice to the noise, going further by revealing a specific, 26th January release date. They also speculated that an official announcement is coming this week alongside the opening of pre-orders. "We've done our own investigation, and our research has paid off. Yes, we've managed to obtain the exact release date of Forza Horizon 6 on PS5," wrote French insider billbil-kun (via machine translation). According to billbil-kun, the game is priced £59.99 in the UK and €69.99 in the rest of Europe. A physical version - with a disc - will also be available at retail. Incidentally, billbil-kun wasn't able to verify whether a Premium Edition is being offered on PS5. On PC and Xbox, the Premium Edition includes an expansion pass, car pass and various other in-game bonuses. If purchased ahead of launch, the Premium Edition also grants up to four days of early access. It's possible Xbox is planning to release a digital-only Premium Edition on PS5, which wouldn't be visible to billbil-kun's typically retail-based sources. Just yesterday, Playground Games issued a statement on X apologising for a general lack of communication about Forza Horizon 6 and assuring players it was listening to feedback. The developer also promised to look into changing the way it communicates with players going forward. Of course, it's always possible the decision to delay Horizon 6 to January was made after Playground announced it was on track for a 2026 release, even though it's been almost exactly one month since. Forza Horizon 6 has been one of the best-selling games this year so far. It continues to attract players each week , and is estimated to be the highest-grossing new release on Steam in 2026 so far . In the Eurogamer Forza Horizon 6 review , Dom Peppiatt said the game has reached the zenith of the Horizon off-shoot spirit despite not really reinventing the wheel.

sources.title: Gears of War: E-Day studio finds a way to get more performance from Xbox Series S - one that other Xbox games could probably use
sources.text: As a first-party Xbox title, Gears of War: E-Day is under pressure to look good and run well on Xbox consoles. This is especially challenging to do on Series S, due to the console's limited computing power compared to Series X. But developer The Coalition has discovered a clever way of circumventing the Series S' limited memory pool. Gears of War: E-Day has densely-detailed environments that require a lot of system memory (RAM), which is a struggle for Xbox Series S' 10GB of GDDR6 RAM. The Coalition's solution was to offload some of that data onto the console's ultra-fast NVMe SSD storage drive. Digital Foundry reported on the tech behind it, which was co-developed by Xbox's Advanced Technology Group. For some context, NVMe SSD drives are made up of RAM modules of their own, so they can act as additional RAM when needed. As fast as they are, however, NVMe drives aren't quite as fast as proper RAM, so The Coalition essentially used the NVMe as a second tier of RAM to help the game's engine stream assets more smoothly. The game then swaps what's needed in the present moment to RAM, and then sends it back to the NVMe when it's not actively being used. "The benefit is that, in exchange for a couple of gigabytes of storage on the SSD, you can gain about a gigabyte of usable system memory," Digital Foundry's report explained. And, the system is smart enough to cherry-pick chunks of data that won't be heavily impacted by being moved to the slower memory. The system uses "advanced heuristics" to decide which data to move to the NVMe, by analysing access patterns. "Frequently used data stays in RAM, and anything idle can move to the SSD," the report added. Whether future Xbox games could use similar technology to increase performance on Xbox Series S is of course the big question, especially as large-world games GTA 6 and Fable approach. But though the execution may be unique to Gears of War: E-Day, the idea of swapping data between slow and fast memory isn't entirely new: Mac devices, for instance, are especially good at doing this. Yet as the current console generation ages, clever solutions will be needed to keep up with demands of triple-A games, especially as this generation may last longer than initially intended thanks to ongoing memory shortages . Incidentally, The Coalition also invested in other engine upgrades throughout E-Day development, such as improving the technology behind gore and dismemberment, because "we had this feeling fans were getting a bit desensitised to the violence in Gears" . It's a potentially important development for Xbox, but it comes at a time when Xbox is in no small amount of disarray as wide-ranging - and ongoing - restructuring rocks Microsoft's gaming division. Staff at The Coalition fear they could be laid off next, following the release of Gears of War: E-Day .

sources.title: Here are our Xbox Game Pass games for October 2026
sources.text: Microsoft has revealed the first batch of games coming to Xbox Game Pass this month, though subscribers only have a week left to try the award-winning Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 before it waves goodbye. October's undisputed headliner is one of last year's hottest games, EA's Battlefield 6 . The large-scale shooter broke series records when it dropped, selling over 7m copies in three days and instantly topping Steam's best-seller charts . Post-launch updates and a surprisingly-involved Top Gun collab have kept the game chugging into this year too, despite layoffs at Battlefield Studios back in March. The other highlights include seven all-new games launching into Game Pass straight away. Time-loop metroidvania Echo Weaver, road trip adventure game Forever Ago, co-op survive-em-up Deep Dish Dungeon, first-person soulslike Valor Mortis, cute photography romp Bluey's Happy Snaps, co-op roguelike Chained Beast, and city-builder (on the back of a space whale) Beyond These Stars slot into the service on the same day as their full launches. But Game Pass giveth and Game Pass taketh away. This month's group of leavers include the widely-acclaimed and hugely-celebrated RPG, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, which debuted on Game Pass early last year. Some personal favorites, like Donut County and Pacific Drive , aren't sticking around either. For more, check out our full guide to Xbox Game Pass and see every game in the service. I have one eyebrow tentatively raised for Deep Dish Dungeon's moody, old-school world, if I can fend off the hordes in Gears of War: E-Day for long enough, that is - are you guys interested in any of the newcomers?
